The agent runs end to end, and every LLM run I can do today is done. All three Gemini reasoning models (3.8, 3.6 and 2.5-flash) are out of free-tier quota after 15, 11 and 18 requests. Quota resets around 12:30 IST tomorrow, when the next evidence runs happen.

All of this is pushed, and every commit carries an Entire checkpoint.

**What works**
- **Full loop:** plan, act, verify, LLM-chosen recovery, self-audit, then a sourced Markdown and HTML report. State is saved every step, and resuming after a crash works (run `1010-bdda52`).
- **Planted errors:** every real-data run caught all 5. The fixture run (Sentry's marketing headcount ×5) caught 6/6: the agreement check failed and the self-audit downgraded the marketing finding.
- **Self-audit:** it overturned the agent's own ML/AI finding in 2 runs and downgraded it in a third. No report has contained an unsourced number.
- **Evidence written up:**
  - two case studies, before and after
  - a recovery table showing each path, natural or injected
  - eval scorecards with trace IDs
  - Entire checkpoint and graph output
  - paid-equivalent unit costs: **$0.0692 of LLM + 20.8 Crustdata credits per run**, n=1
  - `business/inputs.md` for cfo.ai
  - the README draft
  - posts 1–3

**Bugs found from traces and fixed today (one commit each)**
1. Gemini calls had no timeout. Reasoning calls took 120.9 s on average; with a 40 s timeout and fallback they take 6.5 s.
2. Cached LLM calls were counted as spend.
3. A weak ML/AI estimate made the agent throw away 3 of 5 peers. It now keeps 5/5, and Crustdata credits per run dropped from 26.6 to 5.4.
4. The "independent" second opinion reused the same model once Gemini ran out.

Two mistakes of mine: I wrote "143 s" and "7–75×" before checking; the real figures are 120.9 s and 9–32×. Both are corrected wherever I'd written them.

**Still weak, stated plainly in the docs**
- Every before/after comparison is 1 run per side, with different model mixes because of quota. The case studies say so.
- The injected LLM-429 run didn't record whether the fault actually fired. Fired faults are recorded now.
- Malformed-JSON recovery has never come up in a saved run.
- One audit verdict gave a muddled reason. That's a candidate for case study 03.

**Plan after the reset:** 3 same-mix runs per side for the case studies, 4 more evidence runs to make cost-per-run n=5, an evidence-grade fixture eval, and the audit-prompt fix.

**What I need from you:**
- Post #1 (the X handles for Entire and cfo.ai are unverified) and post #2 are drafted in `evidence/build-in-public.md`.
- The Crustdata dollar price per credit, from its billing page. It's the one missing cost input.
- When you build the cfo.ai model, the inputs are in `business/inputs.md`.
- If you can, paste the free-tier limits from AI Studio. Right now the ledger works them out from 429 errors.

input.description: Title classifier eval set
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/akarsh/neatHack — "Spend Radar", a hackathon agent (Python 3.12, run things with `uv run`). It compares a fictional company's people spend with real competitors. Crustdata has no ML/AI role, so the agent estimates ML/AI headcount by LLM-classifying job titles via `spendradar/tools/classify.py` (`classify_titles(titles) -> (dict[title -> {"category","model"}], usage)`; categories: engineering, ml_ai, sales, marketing, other; read the SYSTEM prompt there for definitions).

Your task: build a 30-title hand-labelled eval set and a scorer for that classifier.

1. Collect real job titles from the git-ignored cache: JSON files in cache/crustdata/*.json (job search responses have body.job_listings[].job_details.title; enrich responses have body[0].matches[0].company_data.hiring.recent_titles_csv). Pick 30 distinct titles with a deliberate mix: ~8 clear engineering, ~8 ML/AI (include hard ones like "Applied Scientist", "AI Engineer", "Data Scientist", "MLOps"), ~5 sales (incl. sales engineering / customer success), ~4 marketing, ~5 other (PM, design, finance, intern). Only use titles that actually appear in the cache; if there are not enough ML titles, say so and use fewer — do NOT invent titles.
2. Label each yourself, following the SYSTEM prompt definitions in classify.py exactly. Write evals/titles_labelled.json as a list of {"title", "label", "source_file", "note"} (note = one line for ambiguous cases).
3. Write evals/title_eval.py: loads the set, calls `spendradar.tools.classify.classify_titles` (needs `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv(".env")` first; do NOT init neatlogs), prints per-title correct/incorrect, overall accuracy, ML/AI precision and recall, a confusion summary, and writes evidence/evals/title-classifier-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSS>.json with those numbers plus the model used and the run timestamp.
4. Run it ONCE: `uv run python evals/title_eval.py`. It uses Gemini flash-lite free tier (plenty of quota). Report the real accuracy numbers exactly as printed — never estimate or round up.

Rules: only create evals/titles_labelled.json, evals/title_eval.py and the evidence/evals/title-classifier-*.json output. Do NOT edit any other file, do NOT git add/commit/push, never print API keys. Report back in under 200 words: counts per label, accuracy, ML precision/recall, misclassified titles.

# 03 — Two bugs that only showed up on fallback models

Scorecard: `evidence/evals/20261010T171003-fd9a4ef-gemma-mix-n3.json` (3 evidence runs, commit `fd9a4ef`). All three ran mostly on fallback models (`gemini-3.7-flash` → `gemma-4-31b-it` → OpenRouter `:free`), because the main Flash models were out of free-tier quota.

| Run | Trace | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1010-7d05cb | `6f93a257acc67b3e7df1a245d10673e8` | done, 5/5 planted errors caught, 5/5 peers kept |
| 1010-4c9a03 | `b16cc16a4424fc85ad5478646523ad6e` | done, **4/5**: the mis-categorised invoice finding was wrongly overturned |
| 1010-21b4e0 | `682db8d165a0c041fc26ab495438e142` | **crashed in execute** at step 11 with 37 tasks queued |

## Bug A: a JSON re-ask quietly switched to a weaker model
- **Symptom:** in run 1010-4c9a03, the audit verdict on "Tensorforge GPU billed to [marketing, ml_ai]" was an *overturn* attributed to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. The audit is meant to use the `reason` models.
- **Root cause:** Gemma returned malformed JSON for the verdict, which correctly triggered the JSON re-ask (recovery path 5; its first natural occurrence). But `llm.complete` hard-coded the re-ask to the `extract` role, so the cheapest model re-made the decision.
- **Fix:** the re-ask stays on the same role and honours the same `exclude`. Test: `test_json_reask_stays_on_the_same_role`.

## Bug B: the planner's paths crashed the run
- **Symptom:** in run 1010-21b4e0, every file task failed with `data/acme/data/acme/...: No such file`, and the run then died.
- **Root causes:**
  - Gemma's plan included the input folder in each path, which nothing normalised.
  - `read_pdf(mode="llm")` called `read_bytes()` with no error handling, and the execute loop only caught known error types, so one `FileNotFoundError` ended the process.
- **Fix:** planner paths are normalised (`_normalise_path`), LLM-mode file errors become `ToolError`, and any unexpected exception inside a task is recorded as a tool error and goes through recovery instead of crashing.

- **After:** {{evidence runs on the fixed commit}}
- **Numbers:** n = 3 before (all fallback-heavy, so by our rule not a clean comparison): planted errors caught 5, 4 and 0 (crashed) of 5. After: {{to fill}}.
EOF

- **The mis-categorised invoice was missed in all 3 runs.** The main Gemini Flash models were out of quota, so the backup models (Gemma and Nemotron) did the self-audit. They argued that GPU training hours billed to Marketing were "appropriate" and overturned a correct finding. On Gemini Flash, earlier runs got it right. The self-audit is only as good as the model running it, and the backup models are weaker auditors here.
- **One run skipped the scanned invoice.** No reasoning model was available for that decision, so a fixed fallback rule chose `skip`. For "no text layer" the right default is to re-read the file with the LLM reader.

These runs all leaned on backup models, so by our rule they're indicative, not clean comparisons. Case study 03 says so.

**Next, unless you want something else:**
1. Make "re-read with the LLM reader" the fallback rule for a PDF with no text layer.
2. Make the audit's question more explicit: "do the line items match the cost centre?"
3. When an audit verdict comes from a backup model, label it as lower-trust instead of letting it silently overturn a finding.

Then I'll re-run once Gemini Flash quota resets around 12:30 IST tomorrow, so the comparison uses the stronger models.

toolu_01CBbnovuBcLFGrkJei2ZDcN.prompt: Quote exactly how secret redaction works for transcripts/checkpoints: detection method (entropy? gitleaks rules?), whether custom patterns or local redactors can be added and how (file paths, format, commands), and whether already-pushed checkpoints can be rewritten/removed.

content.content:
**Detection methods**

- **Entropy scoring (layer 1):** Redacts alphanumeric runs of 10 or more characters whose "Shannon entropy exceeds 4.5," replacing them with `REDACTED`.
- **Secret pattern matching (layer 2):** Uses Betterleaks, which "covers several hundred known secret formats," and/or goredact, which "validates a smaller set of provider and contextual token shapes." Betterleaks is the default and goredact is off by default. The page doesn't mention gitleaks. Scanner selection first appears in `v0.10.3-nightly.202608210613.680d64782`, and CLI 0.10.2 uses Betterleaks.
- **Fixed rules:** Provider token prefixes, credentialed URIs, database connection strings, and bounded credential values (layers 3, 4, 5, and 7).
- **Optional layers:** User-defined rules (layer 6), PII detection (layer 8), and the OpenAI Privacy Filter (layer 9, branch backend only, at push time).

Scanner choice is read only from the committed `.entire/settings.json`. Scanner keys in `.entire/settings.local.json` are ignored with a logged warning.

**Custom patterns and local redactors**

- **Inline rules:** Add them under `redaction.custom_redactions` in your settings.
- **Rule packs:** YAML or JSON files under `.entire/redactors/`. Each pack sets a `name` that matches its filename stem, a `version`, and `rules`, each with an `id` and a `regex`. Rules use Go RE2 syntax, so lookarounds and backreferences aren't available.
- **Self-tests:** A rule can include `samples` with `input` and `redacted` expectations, which Entire checks at load time.
- **Personal packs:** Put them in `.entire/redactors/local/`. `entire enable` keeps that directory gitignored.
- **PII patterns:** Add them under `custom_patterns`. Store sensitive ones in `.entire/settings.local.json`.
- **Behavior:** An invalid regex is logged and skipped. Changes take effect on the next CLI or hook invocation, and no reload command exists.

The page doesn't document a CLI command for adding rules. Configuration details are in the Privacy and Redaction guide.

**Already-pushed checkpoints**

The page doesn't describe how to rewrite or remove checkpoints that have already been pushed. The only rewrite it documents is the OPF pre-push pass, which runs before unpushed checkpoint commits reach the remote. Anyone with read access to a repository can read its checkpoints, and a public repository's checkpoints are public. For removal, check the Privacy and Redaction and Session Storage guides, or contact security@entire.io.

content.thinking: Found that Entire's entropy check only flags strings above 4.5 bits, so a 32-hex key (4.0 bits) would slip through. I'll add a local redactor rule in `.entire/redactors/local/` for this key format, plus matching rules in neatlogs masking and the gitleaks hook.

input.command:
mkdir -p .entire/redactors/local && cat > .entire/redactors/local/smallest.yaml <<'EOF'
name: smallest
version: 1
rules:
  - id: smallest-api-key
    regex: 'sk_[0-9a-f]{32}'
    samples:
      - input: "key=REDACTED end"
        redacted: "key=REDACTED end"
EOF
git check-ignore .entire/redactors/local/smallest.yaml && echo "pack is git-ignored"
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='spendradar/tracing.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    "CRUSTDATA_API_KEY",''','''    "CRUSTDATA_API_KEY",
    "SMALLEST_API_KEY",''')
s=s.replace('''    re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),  # AWS access key id''','''    re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),  # AWS access key id
    re.compile(r"sk_[0-9a-f]{32}"),  # smallest (gpt-5-nano)''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='.gitleaks.toml'; s=open(p).read()
s+='''
[[rules]]
id = "smallest-api-key"
description = "smallest API key (sk_ + 32 hex)"
regex = \'\'\'sk_[0-9a-f]{32}\'\'\'
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='.env.example'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("# Crustdata","# smallest — gpt-5-nano (OpenAI-compatible); added 2026-10-10\nSMALLEST_API_KEY=\n\n# Crustdata",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

def test_smallest_key_format_is_scrubbed():

EOF

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Build **Spend Radar** for neatHack (48h, 10 Oct 12:30 IST to 12 Oct 23:55 IST).
     - Team **qwep**, solo builder **Akarsh Dhingra**. Use Akarsh's name everywhere; "Aarav" is a placeholder.
     - The agent compares the fictional Acme Observability Inc.'s people spend with real competitors (via Crustdata), shows sources for every number, and self-audits its findings.
     - It must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, with evidence for each.
   - The user ran /grill-me on the brief. All decisions were recorded into CLAUDE.md (full brief plus the decisions, with the `@.entire/graph-agent.md` import kept at the top).
   - The user then said "You can now Start Building", gave the repo https://github.com/akarsh-dhingra/SpeedRadar-NeetHack, and later said: "Have plugged in all Api keys now you can just keep building , no need to ask from me".
   - Later instructions:
     - Use the AI Studio models shown (screenshot), "you can use others and the openrouter models".
     - Run subagents to divide the work, using sonnet/haiku according to the work and opus only for very complicated work.
     - Use the OpenAI key (gpt-5-nano), which is hackathon-provided: "you can use it as much as you want".
     - Remove all Smallest key stuff from Entire and everywhere.
     - "let me know when the fixture run finishes".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Agent loop.** A plain Python loop: PLAN (LLM typed task list with Pydantic, plus a coverage check), ACT (one tool), OBSERVE (value plus Source), VERIFY (deterministic), DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM picks from a fixed menu via native function calling, or a JSON menu fallback), cross-document checks, FINDINGS (Python maths), SELF-AUDIT (recompute, sources, contradiction evidence, LLM verdict, a second opinion from a different model), REPORT (MD plus HTML with numbered sources).
   - **State and safety.** RunState is saved atomically every step; there's resume; `--crash-after-step` calls `os._exit(137)`; the retry cap is 3; fault injection uses `--inject target:fault` with `fault:injected:*` spans and `faults_fired` recorded.
   - **neatlogs.**
     - `neatlogs.init(api_key, workflow_name, instrumentations=["google_genai","openai"], tags, mask=mask_secrets)`.
     - Spans via `@neatlogs.span(kind=...)` and `neatlogs.trace(name, kind=...)`. Kinds: WORKFLOW, AGENT, CHAIN, TOOL, GUARDRAIL, LLM (trace only).
     - Trace id via `span.get_span_context().trace_id`. session_id = run_id.
     - Tags are process-wide (one process per run).
     - `neatlogs doctor --probe` PASSes. `neatlogs trace get` needs a NEATLOGS_TOKEN (not available).
   - **Entire.**
     - Checkpoints use an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer; refs live at `refs/entire/checkpoints/...` and are pushed on git push.
     - `entire graph search/impact/stats`; `entire checkpoint list/explain`.
     - Redaction: entropy above 4.5 bits, Betterleaks patterns, and rule packs in `.entire/redactors/` (personal packs in `local/`, git-ignored). In a pack sample, `redacted:` is a **bool**.
   - **Crustdata.**
     - Auth: `authorization: Bearer`, `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`.
     - `/company/enrich` costs 2 credits per company. Fields: headcount.by_role_absolute, by_function_timeseries.CURRENT_FUNCTION, timeseries, growth, funding, hiring.recent_titles_csv, news.
     - `/job/search` costs 0.03 per result; `limit:0` group_by aggregations cost 0.
     - `/account/credits` and `/account/endpoints` are free. There is no ML role.
   - **LLMs.**
     - Primary: OpenAI **gpt-5-nano** ($0.05 / $0.40 per 1M, hackathon credits).
     - Gemini free tier, limits from AI Studio:
       - 2.5, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash: 5 RPM, 20 RPD.
       - 3.5 and 3.1 Flash Lite: 15 RPM, 500 RPD.
       - gemma-4-31b-it: 30 RPM, 14.4K RPD, 16K TPM. No function calling (500 error) and slow (38 s).
       - Pro: zero quota.
     - OpenRouter `:free` only (nemotron-3-super, gemma-4) via the guard.
     - Ledger: `cache/ledger.json` tracks requests, tokens and USD per model per day.
   - **Evals and costs.**
     - `ground_truth.json` has 5 planted errors plus a fixture (Sentry Marketing ×5, 19→95).
     - Scorecards include trace ids.
     - Paid-equivalent unit costs = measured tokens × published prices.
   - **Secret scanning.** gitleaks pre-commit hook plus an exact-match check against .env values (`scripts/pre-commit` symlinked into `.git/hooks`).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **CLAUDE.md**
     - Full brief with all decisions.

# cfo.ai inputs: Spend Radar

Akarsh enters these into cfo.ai to build the plan, which must cover **pricing, costs, revenue and runway**. Each line is tagged **MEASURED** (from a real run, with source), **PUBLISHED** (a vendor price, with link and the date I checked it), **PROPOSAL** (a pricing choice we are making), or **ASSUMPTION** (a guess, kept modest and labelled).

## 1. Cost per analysis run

| Input | Value | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLM cost per run (paid-equivalent) | **$0.0285** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) | MEASURED tokens × PUBLISHED prices | `business/unit_costs.md`: 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano ($0.05 / $0.40 per 1M tokens), ~30 LLM calls and ~13K in / ~66K out tokens per run. An earlier Gemini Flash run cost $0.0692 (n = 1) |
| Crustdata credits per run, no cache | **20.8 credits** | MEASURED | 5 competitors × 2 credits (enrich) + 360 job results × 0.03 |
| Crustdata USD per credit | **? (to fill)** | PUBLISHED, not public | Crustdata sells credits in the dashboard: https://app.crustdata.com/billing/credits |
| Hosting, one small instance | ≈ $0.0208/h → **≈ $15.2/month** at 730 h | PUBLISHED (third-party) | instances.vantage.sh/aws/ec2/t3.small, checked 2026-10-10. The page does not confirm region and OS; check the AWS console before relying on it |
| Development spend during the hackathon | **$0** to the team | MEASURED | Gemini free tier, OpenRouter `:free`, hackathon-provided OpenAI and Crustdata credits |

Why paid-equivalent: we developed on free tiers, but a paying customer's runs cannot depend on free quotas. The main model is now gpt-5-nano. If we fall back to Gemini Flash, note that its prices rise on 2027-01-01 (3.6/3.8-flash go from $0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens).

## 2. Usage assumptions

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Runs per customer per month | 8 (weekly refresh × 2 scenarios, e.g. budget-cycle what-ifs) | ASSUMPTION |
| Competitors per run | 5 | MEASURED design default |
| Support/onboarding time per new customer | 2 h | ASSUMPTION |

## 3. Proposed pricing tiers (PROPOSAL)

| Tier | Price / month | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $99 | 1 company, 5 competitors, 8 runs/month, Markdown report |
| Team | $399 | 3 entities, 10 competitors, 40 runs/month, report history, CSV export |
| Enterprise | from $1,500 | SSO, custom policy rules, private deployment (customer data stays off free LLM tiers) |

Per-run variable cost for Starter = 8 × ($0.0285 + 20.8 × Crustdata $/credit). Gross margin depends mainly on the Crustdata credit price, so fill that in first.

## 4. Customer-growth scenarios (ASSUMPTION, deliberately modest)

| Month | Base: paying customers (Starter / Team) | Growth: paying customers (Starter / Team) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 0 (design partners, free) | 0 |
| 6 | 5 / 1 | 10 / 2 |
| 12 | 15 / 3 | 35 / 8 |
| 24 | 40 / 10 | 100 / 25 |

Churn: 3%/month (base), 2%/month (growth). No market-size (TAM) claims.

## 5. Fixed costs and runway (to fill)

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Founder salary | ? | Akarsh |
| Starting cash | ? | Akarsh |
| Tools/SaaS | neatlogs, Crustdata plan, domain: ? | Akarsh |

The cfo.ai plan should output monthly revenue, COGS (LLM + Crustdata + hosting), gross margin, burn, and months of runway under both scenarios. Export it to `business/` when done.

"""LLM title classifier: job title → spend category (ml_ai has no Crustdata role)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

import neatlogs
from pydantic import BaseModel

from spendradar import llm

SYSTEM = (
    "You map job titles to spend categories for a people-cost comparison.\n"
    "engineering: software, infra, SRE, security, data engineering, developer advocacy.\n"
    "ml_ai: roles whose main job is building or researching ML/AI models or ML/AI products "
    "(ML engineer, applied scientist, AI engineer, research scientist, MLOps).\n"
    "sales: AE, SDR/BDR, sales engineering, solutions/pre-sales, partnerships, customer success.\n"
    "marketing: product/growth/brand/content marketing, events, comms.\n"
    "other: everything else (product management, design, finance, HR, ops, support, legal, interns "
    "that do not clearly fit). Classify by the role's work, not by buzzwords in the team name."
)


class TitleLabel(BaseModel):
    title: str
    category: Literal["engineering", "ml_ai", "sales", "marketing", "other"]


class TitleBatch(BaseModel):
    labels: list[TitleLabel]


@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="act:classify_titles", tool_name="classify_titles")
def classify_titles(titles: list[str], batch: int = 40) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], list[dict]]:
    """Returns ({title: {category, model}}, [llm usage per call])."""
    uniq = sorted({t for t in titles if t})
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    usage = []
    for i in range(0, len(uniq), batch):
        chunk = uniq[i:i + batch]
        prompt = "Classify each title. Return every title exactly as given.\n" + "\n".join(f"- {t}" for t in chunk)
        res = llm.complete("extract", prompt, system=SYSTEM, schema=TitleBatch)
        usage.append({"model": res.model, "tokens_in": res.tokens_in, "tokens_out": res.tokens_out,
                      "latency_s": res.latency_s, "cached": res.cached, "reasks": res.reasks})
        # Models echo titles trimmed; match on the stripped form and key by the original title,
        # or titles with stray whitespace (common in Crustdata) are silently dropped.
        by_stripped = {t.strip(): t for t in chunk}
        for lab in res.parsed.labels:
            orig = by_stripped.get(lab.title.strip())
            if orig is not None:
                out[orig] = {"category": lab.category, "model": res.model}
    return out, usage

Base directory for this skill: /Users/akarsh/.claude/skills/grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Word each question so "yes" accepts your recommended answer.

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

ARGUMENTS: # CLAUDE.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

You are building **Spend Radar** with Aarav for **neatHack**, a 48-hour online AI-agent hackathon run by neatlogs. This file is the full brief: the rules, the scoring, what to build, the order to build it, and what evidence to produce. Read all of it before writing code. Re-read the "Hard rules" section whenever you are unsure.

Source of rules: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (fetched 10 Oct 2026). Build-log skill: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill. If anything here conflicts with those pages, the pages win; tell Aarav.

---

## 0. Hard rules (breaking any of these can disqualify us)

1. **All code is written during the hackathon**: Sat 10 Oct 2026, 12:30 PM IST → Mon 12 Oct 2026, 11:55 PM IST. Do not copy in code from any earlier project, including Aarav's other repos (Glance, SecureAgent, etc.). Open-source libraries installed via pip/npm are fine.
2. **Public GitHub repo**, with commits made throughout the event so judges can see the dates. Commit small and often (at least every hour of work). Never squash or rewrite history.
3. **Must use all three: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai**, each with a clear role, and the demo must cover all three.
4. **Demo video ≤ 3 minutes.**
5. **Submission** = a public quote-post on X of the official neatlogs submission post, between **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00 PM and 11:55 PM IST**, containing team name, project name, public repo link, demo link. Late = not judged.
6. **Do not use Glance** or any of Aarav's existing projects in this repo. He wants them kept separate.
7. **No fabricated numbers anywhere** — not in code, README, report, or posts. Every confidence score is computed. Every metric comes from a real run. If something is estimated, label it as an estimate.
8. Never commit secrets. Use `.env` (git-ignored) plus `.env.example`.

---

## 1. Judging (optimise for this, in this order)

| Category | Weight | What the judges look at |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | How well the agent handles a substantial task start to finish |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How effectively they were used to build, improve, and plan a business around the agent |
| Demo video | 20% | How clearly it explains the agent and the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What was shared publicly during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness & originality | 10% | A real problem solved in a new way |

The judges' stated focus areas for the agent: **planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration**. Our design must visibly hit every one.

**Evidence judges require (each claim must be checkable):**
- *Agent improved*: a run before a change and a run after it (two neatlogs traces) with the numbers compared.
- *Used neatlogs*: trace links or screenshots.
- *Used Entire*: checkpoints or entire-graph output from the repo.
- *Used cfo.ai*: a business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway.
- *Recovers from failure*: a run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next.
- *Built c*: links to posts tagged #neatHack.
- *Wrote code during hackathon*: public repo with dated commits.

Judges: 2 from Entire (devrel, solutions engineer), 2 from neatlogs (founder, head of product engineering), 1 founder of Orchestrator.inc. They are engineers who build agent/dev tooling. They will notice fake metrics and they will appreciate real traces, real bugs found and fixed, and clean engineering.

Prizes: 1st $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo credits; 2nd $1,000 + $3,000; 3rd $500 + $1,000; each winner gets 3 months neatlogs Pro. Separate $500 community award for genuine community interest (no bought engagement). Winners announced 16 Oct.

---

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, vendor contracts, a spend policy) and a list of 3–5 competitors (or let the agent pick them).
> Output: a report per spend category (engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing, infra/cloud) with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Positioning for these judges:** use a dev-tools / AI-infra fictional company ("Acme Observability Inc." — clearly labelled fictional) and real dev-tools / AI-infra competitors, so the judges recognise the market.

---

## 3. Tool stack and the role of each tool

| Job | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trace every LLM call, tool call, retry, state change; find bugs; compare runs | **neatlogs** (required) | Read https://docs.neatlogs.com and https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk iring. Integrate before writing agent logic so the very first run is traced. |
| Repo context and checkpoints for the coding agent (you) | **Entire** (required) | https://entire.io — set up checkpoints so each change records its context; run entire-graph once and save the output to `evidence/entire/`. Read its docs first; do not guess commands. |
| Business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway | **cfo.ai** (required) | Aarav signs up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks (card required; cancel subscription immediately in Settings → Billing). He builds the model in cfo.ai; you prepare the inputs (see §9). |
| Competitor data: company info, headcount, job postings, funding | **Crustdata** | 5,000 credits per participant. Docs: https://docs.crustdata.com — Company (search, enrich, identify), Jobs (listings with filters and aggregations), People. **Field availability is NOT confirmed — see §5 Step 1.** |
| LLM | Claude via Anthropic API, or Amazon Bedrock (AWS credits go to the first 200 teams to complete web check-in) | Keep the model call behind one function so it can be swapped. |
| File parsing | `openpyxl` (xlsx), `pdfplumber` (PDF text/tables), Claude PDF input as fallback for scanned PDFs | Test both PDF routes in the first build hour; keep the one that works. |
| Language / framework | Python 3.11+, a plain hand-written agent loop (no heavy framework) | A plain loop is easier to trace, debug, and explain in the demo. Pydantic for state models. |

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop (not a fixed pipeline)

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → add fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan**: LLM reads the goal, file listing, and competitor list; writes a task queue into state (which files to parse, which competitors to fetch, which categories to compare). The plan is a traced span.
2. **Act**: pick the next task, call exactly one tool.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + timestamp).
4. **Verify**: run the deterministic check for that result type (§4.4). On failure, push a fix-up task (re-parse with the other parser, narrow page range, fetch an extra signal, mark low-confidence) and loop. Cap retries per task at 3.
5. **Self-audit** (key differentiator): after all findings exist, a second pass tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks its sources, searches for a contradicting signal (e.g. a hiring freeze or layoffs post), recomputes the number. Findings that fail are downgraded or removed and logged as "overturned".
6. **Report**: write `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (and `report.html`) with every number linked to its source and an "Overturned claims" section.

### 4.2 Tools (functions the agent can call)

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices, contracts |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount, funding, basic info |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles; aggregate by team if supported |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | map job titles → spend category (fallback if no team breakdown) |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual spend |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM plans, classifies, interprets, and writes prose — it never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

# Task

Address the following high-severity issue in this codebase. Read the Context to understand what is failing and why, then apply the changes described in the Fix section. When you need production evidence (real span payloads, errors, timings), use the Neatlogs MCP tools on the trace IDs in References — `get_trace_context` for span detail, `triage_get_investigation` when a thread_id is listed, `triage_get` to reload the fix — do not assume the prompt alone is the full picture.

# Context

## Handle corrupt PDF files in `read_pdf` tool to prevent downstream LLM API errors

**Severity:** High · **Category:** Tool · **Pattern:** Tool contract misuse · **Workflow:** `spendradar` · **Confidence:** 70%
**Status:** Open · **Source:** Auto · **Created:** 2026-10-10 09:47 UTC

## Root cause

The `read_pdf` tool attempts to read PDF files in `mode: "text"` first. When encountering a corrupt PDF file (such as `data/acme/invoices/13_brightloop_2026-10.pdf` which throws `PdfminerException: No /Root object!`), the tool falls back to `mode: "llm"`. However, because the file is fundamentally corrupt and not a valid PDF, passing it to the Gemini LLM (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite` or `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) results in a non-retryable `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error from the Google Generative AI API. This error is not caught gracefully, causing the entire workflow execution to fail.

## Evidence

In trace [View trace](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/36362eb966cdbb85dcb2fb1b280e1034), the `read_pdf` tool fails with `PdfminerException: No /Root object!` on `13_brightloop_2026-10.pdf`. It then attempts to fall back to `mode: "llm"`, which triggers a `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error from `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. Similarly, in trace [View trace](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/6fcb0c5ef827b202df85e61406ca16d8), the same fallback triggers a `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error from `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. This pattern is also confirmed in similar traces such as [View trace](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/af0df27e2d3433e0c608fb28a018a22d) (started Oct 10 08:33 UTC) and [View trace](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/288f07d84bb84e15754a241eef40d779) (started Oct 10 08:39 UTC).

## Confidence breakdown

| Signal | Score |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence strength | 95% |
| Pattern consistency | 95% |
| Detection alignment | 90% |
| Expected impact | 90% |

# Fix

## Recommended action

## Pre-validate PDF files and handle LLM API errors gracefully in `read_pdf` tool

**Steps**

1. Modify the `read_pdf` tool implementation to check if the PDF file is valid before attempting fallback modes.
2. If `pdfplumber` throws a `PdfminerException: No /Root object!` or similar corruption error, do not attempt to fall back to `mode: "llm"`. Instead, immediately return a clear, structured error indicating that the PDF file is corrupt.
3. Add a `try-except` block around the LLM PDF reader call to catch `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` or other API errors, and return a friendly error message instead of letting the exception bubble up and crash the workflow.

**Verificatio a test script passing a corrupt PDF (e.g., missing `/Root` object) to `read_pdf` and verify it returns a structured error instead of throwing a `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` exception.
- Run the `spendradar_run` workflow with the test data and verify it completes successfully or handles the corrupt file gracefully.

**Risk assessment**

Low risk. This only changes error handling and validation inside the `read_pdf` tool, preventing unhandled exceptions.

**Rollback plan**

Revert the changes to the `read_pdf` tool implementation in the codebase.

# References

This fix is linked to 8 production traces.

## MCP identifiers

Use these with the Neatlogs MCP server (if connected in the IDE):

- **triage_id:** `2cd5e9df-86d1-4a85-977d-94ebb059615e` → `triage_get`, `triage_list_steps`, `triage_update_status`, `triage_update`, `triage_dismiss`

Once work on this fix is done, update its status on Neatlogs so the team's board stays accurate. Fix ID: `2cd5e9df-86d1-4a85-977d-94ebb059615e`.

# CLAUDE.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

You are building **Spend Radar** with Akarsh (team **qwep**, solo) for **neatHack**, a 48-hour online AI-agent hackathon run by neatlogs. This file is the full brief: the rules, the scoring, what to build, the order to build it, and what evidence to produce. Read all of it before writing code. Re-read "Hard rules" whenever you are unsure.

Source of rules: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (fetched 10 Oct 2026). Build-log skill: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill. If anything here conflicts with those pages, the pages win; tell Akarsh.

---

## 0. Hard rules (breaking any of these can disqualify us or cost money)

1. **All code is written during the hackathon**: Sat 10 Oct 2026, 12:30 PM IST → Mon 12 Oct 2026, 11:55 PM IST. Do not copy in code from any earlier project, including Akarsh's other repos (Glance, SecureAgent, etc.). Open-source libraries installed via pip/npm are fine.
2. **Public GitHub repo**, with commits made throughout the event so judges can see the dates. Commit small and often (at least every hour of work). Never squash or rewrite history. The repo's first commit must be after 12:30 PM IST, 10 Oct.
3. **Must use all three: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai**, each with a clear role, and the demo must cover all three.
4. **Demo video ≤ 3 minutes** (not stated on the rules page; we keep it as the safe limit).
5. **Submission** = a public quote-post on X of the official neatlogs submission post, between **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00 PM and 11:55 PM IST**, containing team name (qwep), project name, public repo link, demo link. Late = not judged.
6. **Do not use Glance** or any of Akarsh's existing projects in this repo.
7. **No fabricated numbers anywhere** — not in code, README, report, posts, or the video. Every confidence score is computed. Every metric comes from a saved scorecard or trace link. Unmeasured numbers in drafts are written as `{N}` placeholders and filled only from a real run. Estimates are labelled as estimates.
8. **Never commit secrets.** `.env` (git-ignored) plus `.env.example`. Secrets never appear in commits, logs, neatlogs traces, or screenshots (see §6.1).
9. **Zero spend, everywhere.** No billing on any service. Free tiers only for LLMs (§3). Never add credits or a payment method to OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, or anything else. cfo.ai is cancelled in Settings → Billing immediately after signup. AWS use stays inside the organisers' allowance and instances are stopped whenever idle. Anything that could incur a charge → ask Akarsh first.
10. **Real customer finance data never goes through free LLM providers.** We only send fictional Acme data and public Crustdata facts.

---

## 1. Judging (optimise for this, in this order)

| Category | Weight | What the judges look at |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | How well the agent handles a substantial task start to finish |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How effectively they were used to build, improve, and plan a business around the agent |
| Demo video | 20% | How clearly it explains the agent and the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What was shared publicly during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness & originality | 10% | A real problem solved in a new way |

Focus areas for the agent: **planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration**. The design must visibly hit every one.

**Evidence judges require (each claim must be checkable):**
- *Agent improved*: runs before and after a change (neatlogs traces) with numbers compared (§7).
- *Used neatlogs*: trace links or screenshots.
- *Used Entire*: checkpoints or entire-graph output from the repo.
- *Used cfo.ai*: a business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway.
- *Recovers from failure*: a run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next.
- *Built in public*: links to posts tagged #neatHack.
- *Wrote code during hackathon*: public repo with dated commits.

Judges: 2 from Entire (devrel, solutions engineer), 2 from neatlogs (founder, head of product engineering), 1 founder of Orchestrator.inc. They build agent/dev tooling. They will notice fake metrics and will appreciate real traces, real bugs found and fixed, and clean engineering.

Prizes: 1st $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo credits; 2nd $1,000 + $3,000; 3rd $500 + $1,000; each winner gets 3 months neatlogs Pro. Separate $500 community award for genuine community interest. Winners announced 16 Oct.

---

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, spend policy) and a hard-coded competitor list (`data/acme/competitors.yaml`).
> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**
- **Competitor comparison is on people cost only**: engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing *team*. Each category states "people cost only" in the report. Policy rules in `policy.yaml` are written against people cost.
- **Infra/cloud** is checked only internally (our invoices vs budget vs policy). No competitor estimate for it.

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. Step 1 probes 7 candidates — Datadog, Grafana Labs, Chronosphere, Honeycomb, Arize, New Relic, Sentry — and keeps the 4–5 with the best Crustdata coverage. Never include neatlogs or Entire (their people judge). Competitor auto-selection is a stretch goal only.

**Our company:** "Acme Observability Inc." — fictional, labelled as such everywhere.

---

## 3. Tool stack and the role of each tool

| Job | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trace every LLM call, tool call, retry, decision, state change; find bugs; compare runs | **neatlogs** (required) | Docs: https://docs.neatlogs.com, https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk. Integrate before agent logic so the first run is traced. Details in §6. |
| Repo context and checkpoints for the coding agent (you) | **Entire** (required) | Already enabled for Claude Code (`entire enable --agent claude-code`; re-run after any `git init`). Checkpoints add an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer to commits. Evidence: `entire checkpoint list/explain`, `entire graph stats`, entire-graph output → `evidence/entire/`. |
| Business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway | **cfo.ai** (required) | Akarsh signs up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks and cancels the subscription immediately. He builds the model; you prepare inputs (§9). |
| Competitor data | **Crustdata** | 5,000 credits. Auth: `authorization: Bearer <key>`, `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`. `POST /company/enrich` (`fields`: headcount incl. `by_role_absolute`/`by_role_percent`, growth `mom/qoq/six_months/yoy/two_years`; funding) ≈ 2 credits/company. `POST /job/search` (`job_details.title`, `job_details.category`, `metadata.date_added`; `group_by` aggregations, `limit:0` for aggregation-only) at 0.03 credits/result. No headcount timeseries — trend comes from growth fields. Confirm all fields with the Step 1 probe; check real prices via `GET /account/endpoints`. |
| LLM — primary | **Google Gemini, free tier only** (`google-genai>=1.55.0`) | Role split: Pro → plan, `decide:recovery`, self-audit; Flash → report prose; Flash-Lite → extraction, title classification, JSON re-asks. **Read the real model list and rate limits from AI Studio in Step 2; do not trust model names from memory.** If Pro's daily quota is too small, the eval decides whether Flash is good enough for planning (becomes a case study). |
| LLM — secondary | **OpenRouter, `:free` models only** | Never add credits. A guard in `llm.py` refuses any model ID not ending in `:free`. Free limits without credits: 20 req/min, 50 req/day. Roles: (1) cross-provider failover after Gemini retries + model fallback are exhausted; (2) independent second opinion in the self-audit, max 5 calls/run, only on findings Gemini marked uncertain or overturned. Pick the model in Step 2 by listing free models via the API; it must support JSON output or tool calling and pass our Pydantic schemas. |
| Hosting (optional) | **AWS** | Organisers' allowance ($25, us-east-1 only) covers EC2, Lambda, IAM and load balancers only; Bedrock is not available. One instance, t3.micro or t3.small, in Hackathon_VPC, for a live report / scheduled runs. Stop it whenever not needed (the access page does not track spend). Never on the critical path. AWS keys stay in `.env` and never appear in commits, logs, traces or screenshots. |
| File parsing | `openpyxl` (xlsx), `pdfplumber` (PDF), Gemini PDF input as fallback for scanned PDFs | Test both PDF routes early; keep the one that works. |
| Language | Python 3.11+, plain hand-written loop, Pydantic for state | No heavy agent framework. |

All LLM calls go through one module, `llm.py`: `llm(role=..., ...)` picks the model per role, enforces the `:free` guard, the rate limiter, and the quota ledger, and records provider/model on every span.

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

---

## 5. Build order (commit after each numbered step)

All times IST. If behind schedule, see §11.

### Saturday 10 Oct — working skeleton by midnight

**Step 0 (before 12:30, no code):** Akarsh does web check-in, Luma, Discord, cfo.ai signup + immediate cancel. Plan and read docs only.

**Step 1 — Repo + Crustdata spike (12:30–1:15, ≤ 25 credits):**
- Reset local git (the pre-12:30 `.git` is discarded — confirm with Akarsh before deleting), `git init`, re-run `entire enable --agent claude-code`, push to a new empty public repo. First commit: this CLAUDE.md, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`.
- `spikes/crustdata_probe.py`: enrich + jobs `group_by job_details.category` (`limit:0`) for the 7 candidates; raw JSON to `cache/`. Report exactly which fields exist. Pick the 4–5 best-covered → `data/acme/competitors.yaml`.
- **Decision by 2:00 PM:** role-level headcount exists → use directly; only totals + titles → `classify_titles` + 30-title labelled eval set; neither usable → stop and tell Akarsh.

**Step 2 — Instrumentation + providers (by 2:30, may run to 3:00):**
- neatlogs `init()` with `instrumentations=["google_genai"]`, the `mask` callback (§6.1), and run tags. One traced dummy Gemini call visible in the dashboard. Check whether `neatlogs sharing` can produce public trace links; if not, evidence uses screenshots.
- List real Gemini models + rate limits from AI Studio; list OpenRouter `:free` models via API and pick one that passes our schemas. Write the limits into `config.yaml` and the ledger.
- Secret-masking unit test passes (required before Step 2 counts as done).
- gitleaks pre-commit hook (§6.1), added alongside Entire's hooks; verify the Entire checkpoint trailer still appears.
- **Plan the case studies:** from the real quotas, work out how many before/after comparisons (n=3 runs per side, §7) fit in the remaining days, and write that plan into `hackathon.md` before running any.

**Step 3 — Sample data (by 4:00):** under `data/acme/` (fictional, labelled):
- `budget_fy27.xlsx` — spend by category × month
- `invoices/` — 12–15 PDFs incl. **one scanned-image PDF, one corrupt file, one whose line items don't sum to its total, one mis-categorised**
- `policy.yaml` — people-cost rules, e.g. "ML/AI team cost within 20% of competitor median"
- `salary_table.csv` — loaded cost per role category (cite a public source or label as assumption)
- `competitors.yaml` — from Step 1
- `ground_truth.json` — planted errors and correct totals (evals only, never shown to the agent)

**Step 4 — Tools (by 7:00):** §4.2 tools + `llm.py`, unit tests for the deterministic ones.

**Step 5 — Loop + state (by 10:00):** plan → act → observe → verify → decide, state saved per step; end-to-end run with a rough report.

**Step 6 — First full traced run (by midnight):** trace link → `evidence/traces.md`. Draft post #2.

### Sunday 11 Oct — trustworthy and measurable

**Step 7 — Verification + computed confidence.**
**Step 8 — Recovery paths (§4.5):** collect natural failure traces; inject the rest; save links.
**Step 9 — Eval harness (§7):** `python -m spendradar eval [--n 3]` → scorecard.
**Step 10 — Find real bugs in neatlogs traces** (hallucinated totals, wasted retries, token blow-ups, wrong tool choice, slow spans). Fix 2–3, within the case-study plan from Step 2. Each → `evidence/case-studies/NN-<slug>.md`.
**Step 11 — Self-audit pass:** measure overturn rate on planted errors and fixtures.
**Step 12 — Resume-after-crash** (kill mid-run, resume, finish). Save trace.
**Step 13 — Cost per run:** tokens/latency per model from neatlogs for 5 runs → `business/unit_costs.md` as paid-equivalent cost (§9).
**Sunday night:** record a backup demo video.

### Monday 12 Oct — package and submit

**Step 14 (by noon):** README (§10), report polish, architecture diagram (Mermaid + PNG).
**Step 15 (by 3 PM):** cfo.ai plan finalised by Akarsh, exported to `business/`.
**Step 16 (by 5 PM):** final demo video, captioned, uploaded (YouTube unlisted or Loom), ≤ 3:00.
**Step 17 (6:30 PM):** final commit, all README links verified.
**Step 18 (7:00 PM sharp):** Akarsh quote-posts the official neatlogs post (aim for the first 50).

---

## 6. neatlogs usage (25% category — central, not decorative)

- Install `neatlogs[google-genai]`; call `neatlogs.init(...)` **before** constructing the Gemini client. OpenRouter calls get custom spans (or an instrumentation key if verified in docs).
- Trace every LLM call (prompt, response, tokens, model, provider), every tool call (`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", ...)`), every retry, every `decide:recovery`, every `fallback:<model>`, verification results, self-audit verdicts. Span kinds per https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/span-kinds.
- Span names: `plan`, `act:read_pdf`, `verify:totals`, `decide:recovery`, `fallback:<model>`, `audit:finding_<id>`, `report`.
- Tags are process-wide, so each `spendradar run` is its own process with tags `sha:<short-sha>`, `run:<run_id>`, `variant:<label>`, plus `evidence` / `inject:<...>` / `fixture` when applicable.
- neatlogs has no run-comparison feature we found; our eval scorecards store trace IDs and our table does the comparison. Use neatlogs evals/experiments features only per docs; never invent APIs.
- Every bug fix starts from a trace link and ends with comparison traces.

### 6.1 Secret safety

- Client-side `mask` callback in `neatlogs.init(mask=...)`: blank attributes whose key contains key/secret/token/password; regex-mask key formats (`AIza…`, `sk-or-…`, `AKIA…`, `Bearer …`, Crustdata key) in all text values; mask every secret value loaded from `.env`. Do not change server-side PII settings (they are project-wide).
- Unit test: a fake key through a span comes out masked.
- Pre-commit: gitleaks (open source) via `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, appended to Entire's hook, with custom rules for Crustdata and OpenRouter key formats.

## 7. Evals (turn "it improved" into a number)

`ground_truth.json` lists planted errors (mismatched totals, mis-categorised invoice, corrupt file) and correct category totals, plus the fault-injected fixtures.

**Fixtures rule:** Altered fixtures are allowed only in `evals/`, and every run report labels whether it used real data or a fixture. Fixtures in `evals/fixtures/` are cached real Crustdata responses with one field changed on purpose (e.g. ML job postings × 5), each logged in `ground_truth.json`. Product runs only ever read real data. `--fixtures` refuses any folder outside `evals/`, tags the run `fixture`, and sets the report's data mode to FIXTURE.

The eval reports:
- planted errors caught / total
- category total accuracy (abs % error)
- unsupported numbers in report (target 0)
- planted/fixture false findings overturned by self-audit / total (scored)
- competitor findings overturned on real data: N (no ground truth — unscored; report shows both sources side by side)
- title-classifier accuracy on 30 labelled titles (only if used)
- tokens, requests, latency per run, per model; `provider_mix`

**Comparisons:** each side of a before/after = 3 runs with the same provider mix; runs that used fallback are excluded. Report mean and min–max; link one trace per side and list all in the case study. If quota allows fewer than 3, say so — never round up. Check the ledger before starting.

Scorecards → `evidence/evals/<timestamp>-<sha>.json` (including trace IDs); improvement table in `evidence/evals/README.md`.

## 8. Evidence folder

```
evidence/
  traces.md                 # every important trace link, one line each, with what it shows
  case-studies/NN-<slug>.md
  recovery/                 # per recovery path: trace link/screenshot, natural or injected
  evals/                    # scorecards + improvement table
  entire/                   # checkpoint list/explain output, entire graph stats, graph output
  build-in-public.md        # every #neatHack post, with timestamp and link
```

Case-study template:
```
# <Bug title>
- Symptom (what the trace showed): <trace link before>
- Root cause:
- Fix: <commit link>
- After: <trace link after>
- Numbers (n=<runs> per side, same provider mix): <metric before mean [min–max]> → <after mean [min–max]>
```

## 9. cfo.ai inputs (you prepare; Akarsh enters them)

`business/inputs.md`:
- **Paid-equivalent cost per run**: measured tokens per model (neatlogs) × the published paid price of the same model, with price-page link and date checked. Labelled as an estimate; development ran on free tiers, but paying customers can't.
- Crustdata credits per run (measured) and their cost at a cited public price (or labelled assumption).
- Runs per customer per month (assumption), hosting estimate, proposed pricing tiers (labelled proposals), base and growth customer scenarios.
- Modest, explicit assumptions; no unsupported TAM claims. The plan must cover **pricing, costs, revenue, runway**.

## 10. README structure

1. One-liner + 20-second GIF of a run
2. The problem (3 sentences)
3. What the agent does end to end
4. Architecture diagram + the loop
5. Each focus area (planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration) — one line + one trace link each
6. How we used neatlogs / Entire / cfo.ai — one section each with evidence links
7. Results: eval improvement table, case studies
8. Run it yourself (setup, `.env`, `python -m spendradar run data/acme`, `resume`, `eval`, `ledger`)
9. Limitations: estimates; people cost only; fictional company data; Crustdata coverage; developed on free LLM tiers which may use prompts for training (only fictional/public data was sent); business costs are paid-equivalent estimates
10. Built during neatHack, 10–12 Oct 2026 — links to build-in-public posts

## 11. If behind schedule — cut in this order

1. HTML report (keep Markdown)
2. Resume-after-crash
3. Competitor auto-selection (already a stretch goal)

Already cut: contracts parsing (return only if ahead on Sunday 6 PM).

**Never cut:** neatlogs tracing, verification, at least one recovery trace, at least one before/after case study, eval scorecard, cfo.ai plan, Entire evidence, the video, the posts.

Cut entirely: Slack alerts, custom dashboards, mock competitor data in product runs, hand-typed confidence scores, any demo longer than 3 minutes.

## 12. Building in public (15%) — draft these for Akarsh

Draft each post in `evidence/build-in-public.md` when its moment arrives; Akarsh posts them. Every post: #neatHack, tag @neatlogs where natural, a real screenshot, and only numbers from saved scorecards/traces.

1. Sat ~1 PM — the idea + the loop sketch
2. Sat night — first full traced run
3. Sun morning — a bug the traces caught
4. Sun afternoon — eval scorecard across commits
5. Sun night — self-audit overturning its own wrong claims
6. Mon — cfo.ai unit economics built from real trace token counts
7. Mon 7:00 PM — submission quote-post (team qwep, project, repo, demo)

Also genuinely help other teams in Discord and on X.

## 13. Demo video script (≤ 3:00, covers all three tools)

| Time | Show | Say |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:15 | Self-audit overturning a claim in a trace, with the scorecard on screen | "This agent caught {N} of its own mistakes before reporting them." (N from the final scorecard; if N = 1: "Here's the moment it caught itself.") |
| 0:15–0:40 | Architecture diagram; run starts | Problem; the loop; tools |
| 0:40–1:20 | **neatlogs**: failure → `decide:recovery` (a non-default choice) → recovery; before/after case study; eval table | The bug we found in traces and the numbers after the fix |
| 1:20–1:45 | **Entire**: checkpoints / entire-graph | How context was kept across the coding agent's changes |
| 1:45–2:20 | **cfo.ai**: plan built from measured tokens → paid-equivalent cost | Pricing, costs, revenue, runway |
| 2:20–2:50 | Final report with source links, data-mode header | Result + usefulness |
| 2:50–3:00 | Repo + #neatHack | Close |

Captions on. Every number on screen must come from a saved scorecard or trace.

## 14. Working agreements for Claude Code

- Before using any external SDK/API (neatlogs, Entire, Crustdata, cfo.ai, Gemini, OpenRouter, AWS), read its current docs; never guess function names or model IDs. If docs are unclear, write a tiny probe and inspect real output.
- Timestamps in `hackathon.md`, `evidence/` and posts come from `date` or commit times, never estimated.
- Keep `hackathon.md` at the repo root per the neatHack skill: sections Project, Team, Stack, Build log, Demo, Limitations, Submission. Append a dated entry per work session separating planned vs done and listing tests actually run; never delete old entries; no secrets, private traces, or made-up results.
- Commit messages: imperative, specific, with step number (e.g. `step 8: add backoff+cache fallback for crustdata 429`).
- Ask Akarsh before: switching ideas, spending > 100 Crustdata credits in one go, anything that could cost money, starting/leaving an AWS instance running, or anything irreversible.
- Small, working, traced increments over big rewrites. Every evening main runs end to end.
- When reporting progress, lead with what works, what's broken, and the next decision needed.
- Open decision: whether neatlogs public trace links work (resolve in Step 2).

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

Step 1 probes 7 candidates — Datadog, Grafana Labs, Chronosphere, Honeycomb, Arize, New Relic, Sentry — and keeps the 4–5 with the best Crustdata coverage. Never include neatlogs or Entire (their people judge). Competitor auto-selection is a stretch goal only.

All LLM calls go through one module, `llm.py`: `llm(role=..., ...)` picks the model per role, enforces the `:free` guard, the rate limiter, and the quota ledger, and records provider/model on every span.

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.
